notes:
Segment covers Uttar Pradesh (st-up), Uttarakhand (st-uk), Himachal Pradesh (st-hp) completely except districts (owned by local-lgd; referenced only as st-<code>-dist-* where needed — none created here) and the High Courts serving them (owned by judiciary segment: in-hc-allahabad for UP, Uttarakhand High Court and Himachal Pradesh High Court for UK/HP — referenced, not defined).

Known gaps / low-confidence items flagged individually via confidence="low" on the relevant position, but summarized here:
- UP State Election Commissioner (Manoj Kumar, since Jan 2018) — source is a stale 2018 report; UP SEC commissioners serve up to 6 years, so this holder is very likely outdated by 2026. NOT independently re-verified.
- UP Lokayukta (Sanjay Mishra, since Jan 2016) — same concern; a decade-long tenure is implausible for a role with a statutory term, likely stale on Wikipedia. NOT independently re-verified.
- UP Public Service Commission chair (Sanjay Shrinet) — no appointment date found.
- UP Legislative Council Deputy Chairman — not found in the source used; left unlisted rather than invented.
- Himachal Pradesh Chief Secretary (Kamlesh Kumar Pant) and DGP (Ashok Tiwari, acting) — no appointment dates found; DGP explicitly marked "acting" per source.
- Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh State Election Commissioners, Public Service Commission chairs, Lokayuktas and State Human Rights Commission chairs were NOT located within the research budget (heavy Wikipedia API rate-limiting from concurrent research agents constrained the number of lookups that could be completed) — omitted rather than invented. Should be filled in a follow-up pass.
- Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh municipal corporation mayors were not verified (UP's are, from the same source table) — the schema permits omitting mayor/commissioner names when not easily verifiable; the corporation entities themselves and their counts (11 for UK, 8 for HP) are sourced.
- UP's council of ministers list (60 seats total per the "party strength of ministry" table on Wikipedia) is reproduced here with 35 currently-serving individual portfolio-holders extracted (21 cabinet incl. CM+2 Deputy CMs, 16 MoS-Independent-Charge, 21 MoS — note the union of these three groups is 58; two additional entries referenced in the source table as having "Made MoS(I/C)" transitions were folded into their later MoS(I/C) row rather than duplicated). One vacancy is known and unresolved on Wikipedia: Jitin Prasada (PWD) left office 2024-06-11 with no listed successor in the source table — PWD portfolio holder after that date is unconfirmed.
- All Governor/CM/Deputy-CM/Speaker/LoP holders were cross-checked against dedicated Wikipedia infobox/list pages as of the 2026-09-25 as-of date; the Himachal Pradesh Governor change (Kavinder Gupta, March 2026) has an additional dated press citation (The Hindu, 6-7 March 2026).
- Population figures use Census of India 2011 final totals per the schema's `population2011` field (UP 199,812,341; Uttarakhand 10,086,292; Himachal Pradesh 6,864,602) rather than the larger 2021/2025 projected estimates shown on current Wikipedia infoboxes, per the schema's own field name.
- Tooling note: the shared Wikipedia MediaWiki API was heavily rate-limited during this run (many concurrent research segments hitting it at once); WebFetch and paced/retried curl were used as workarounds, which slowed but did not block completion.


--- Adversarial verification pass (2026-09-25) ---
Added Uttarakhand SEC (Sushil Kumar), Uttarakhand PSC (Gajendra Joshi), Uttarakhand Lokayukta (A P Subba), Himachal Pradesh SEC (Anil Kumar Khachi), Himachal Pradesh PSC (Rameshwar Singh Thakur, low confidence — citation looked stale), Uttar Pradesh SHRC (Bala Krishna Narayana), Uttarakhand SHRC (Akhilesh Chandra Sharma). Himachal Pradesh Lokayukta and Himachal Pradesh SHRC current holders could not be confirmed (English Wikipedia gives no name for either) and were left out rather than invented — a genuine open gap for a future pass with official-portal access. HP Chairman Rameshwar Singh Thakur is flagged low-confidence for the same reason.
